environment: Glacial conditions and lower sea level expose continental shelves. African moisture patterns vary regionally.
people_plants: Foragers use changing mosaics of terrestrial and coastal resources, including the Palaeo-Agulhas Plain.

environment: Deglaciation changes temperature, coastlines and monsoon strength. Wetter conditions develop across parts of northern Africa.
people_plants: Changing water and vegetation distributions alter routes and access to wild plant and animal foods.

environment: The Holocene begins. Lakes and grasslands expand in parts of the Sahara and neighbouring regions.
people_plants: Gathering, hunting and fishing persist. Food-production histories differ among regions and communities.

environment: Humid northern landscapes support lakes, wetlands and grazing. Conditions are not uniform across Africa.
people_plants: Pastoralism develops alongside foraging and fishing; communities combine resources in different ways.

environment: The African Humid Period ends at different times across regions as monsoonal rain retreats.
people_plants: Mobility, herding and cultivation change as access to water and grazing shifts. Crop domestication is regionally distinct.

environment: Regional vegetation and rainfall changes affect routes through forests and savannas.
people_plants: Bantu-speaking communities continue spreading. Mixed farming, ironworking and local exchanges reshape plant use.

environment: Regional wet and dry phases alter growing conditions; local records need separate interpretation.
people_plants: Mapungubwe and Great Zimbabwe link farming, livestock and trade. Climate is one influence on social change.

environment: African expressions of the Little Ice Age differ among regions, including major drought episodes.
people_plants: Crop diversity, storage, exchange and movement help communities respond, with unequal resources and outcomes.

environment: Industrial carbon emissions rise globally while African environments undergo major land-use changes.
people_plants: Colonial land policies and commercial crops alter livelihoods alongside existing farming and pastoral systems.

environment: Instrumental records show sustained global warming. Heat and water stress vary across African regions.
people_plants: Crop choices, water management and livelihood diversity remain central. Current global measurements are examined in Lecture 5.
